title: Website cookie notice
blurb: A short, honest notice about cookies and similar tracking on your site.

fields.label: Where the parties are based
fields.help: Used for the notes at the end. It does not make the text fit local law.

fields.label: Essential cookies you use
fields.default: a session cookie to keep you signed in; a security cookie to prevent forged requests; a cookie remembering your cookie choices

fields.label: Analytics or optional cookies (leave empty if none)
fields.placeholder: privacy-friendly analytics that count visits without identifying you

fields.label: How people change their choice
fields.default: using the "Cookie settings" link in the footer, or through your browser settings

clauses.heading: About this notice
clauses.text: This notice explains how **{{company}}** uses cookies and similar technologies on {{site}}. It applies from {{effective_date}}.
clauses.note: Keep it short and specific to your site.

clauses.heading: What cookies are
clauses.text: Cookies are small text files a website stores on your device. Similar technologies include local storage and pixels. Some are needed for the site to work; others help us understand how it is used.
clauses.note: A plain explanation for non-technical readers.

clauses.heading: Essential cookies
clauses.text: We use these cookies because the site cannot work properly without them: {{essential}}. These do not need your consent in most places.
clauses.note: List each essential cookie and what it does.

clauses.heading: Optional cookies
clauses.text: We also use: {{analytics}}. Where the law requires, we set these only after you agree, and you can change your mind at any time.
clauses.note: If you have no optional cookies, say so plainly instead.

clauses.heading: No optional cookies
clauses.text: We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.
clauses.note: Delete this if you add optional cookies later.

clauses.heading: Your choices
clauses.text: You can change your cookie choices {{manage}}. Blocking essential cookies may stop parts of the site from working.
clauses.note: Make changing choices as easy as giving consent.

clauses.heading: Contact
clauses.text: Questions? Email {{contact_email}}. For how we handle personal data generally, see our privacy policy.

jurisdiction.US: There is no single federal cookie law, but state privacy laws may require notice and opt-out of certain tracking or "sale/sharing" of data. Rules differ from state to state. Some states limit certain clauses (for example non-competes or how far liability can be limited). Choose the state whose law governs and check how it treats each clause.
jurisdiction.UK: Consent is generally required before non-essential cookies; the regulator publishes guidance on what counts as essential. England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate legal systems. Consumer protection and unfair-terms rules can override clauses in contracts with consumers.
jurisdiction.EU: Prior consent is generally required for non-essential cookies, and rejecting should be as easy as accepting. Each EU country has its own contract law on top of EU-wide rules (such as data protection and consumer rights). Mandatory local rules can apply whatever the contract says, and a translation may be needed.
jurisdiction.CA: Contract law is mostly provincial, and Quebec follows a civil-law system with its own rules, including on the language of contracts. Federal and provincial privacy laws may both apply.
jurisdiction.AU: The Australian Consumer Law applies across the country and can make some terms in standard-form contracts unfair and void. States and territories also have their own rules.
jurisdiction.Other: Laws vary widely. Have a lawyer where the parties are based check every clause, including whether the agreement needs witnesses, stamps, notarising or a particular language to be valid.
